# Sirach Chapter 48 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 48 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Council Notes

Sirach 48 opens with what is arguably the most memorable line in the entire Praise of the Ancestors: "Elijah arose like fire, and his word burned like a torch" (v. 1). This line must be rendered with full force. The chapter covers Elijah (vv. 1–11), Elisha (vv. 12–14), the Northern Kingdom's fall (vv. 15–16), and Hezekiah and Isaiah (vv. 17–25).

**Key decisions:**
- v. 1: "arose like fire" — all three agents render this nearly identically. "Like fire" must not be softened. SOPHIA preserves without change.
- v. 10: The allusion to Mal. 4:5–6 (Elijah's eschatological return) must be preserved. "To calm wrath before it burns hot" and "to turn the heart of the father to the son."
- v. 11: "fall asleep in love" (EMET) vs. "fallen asleep in love" (LOGOS) — Greek kekoimēmenoi en agapē. The beatitude structure (makarios + those who die in love) requires careful rendering. What does "in love" mean? Love of Elijah? Love of God? The ambiguity is intentional.
- v. 12: "wrapped in the whirlwind" (EMET) vs. "enveloped in the whirlwind" (LOGOS) — Greek kaluphtheis = covered, wrapped. "Wrapped" is more precise.
- v. 13: "from wherever he had lain, his body prophesied" (EMET) — refers to Elisha's bones raising a dead man (2 Kings 13:21). This extraordinary statement must stand.
- v. 17: "bored through the rock" — Hezekiah's tunnel (2 Kings 20:20; cf. Siloam inscription).
- v. 18: "Rabshakeh" — retain the personal name as in the historical account (2 Kings 18).
- v. 21: "messenger" (EMET) vs. "angel" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) — Greek angelos. SOPHIA adopts "angel" as the standard English for divine messenger.
- v. 24: "a great spirit" vs. "by the power of the spirit" — this refers to Isaiah's prophetic inspiration. "Great spirit" (EMET) is ambiguous; "power of the spirit" (PNEUMA) is interpretive; SOPHIA adopts "by a great spirit" as preserving the ambiguity between the divine spirit and Isaiah's own greatness.

---

**48:1** Then Elijah arose like fire, and his word burned like a torch.

**48:2** He brought famine upon them, and by his zeal he reduced their number.

**48:3** By the word of the Lord he shut up the heavens, and three times called down fire.

**48:4** How glorious you were, O Elijah, in your wondrous deeds! Who has the right to boast as you do?

**48:5** You who raised a dead man from death, from Hades, by the word of the Most High;

**48:6** who brought kings down to ruin and men of honor from their beds;

**48:7** who heard rebuke at Sinai and judgments of vengeance at Horeb;

**48:8** who anointed kings to execute vengeance and prophets as successors after you;

**48:9** who were taken up in a whirlwind of fire, in a chariot with horses of fire;

**48:10** who are appointed for the end times to calm wrath before it burns hot, to turn the heart of the father to his son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.

**48:11** Blessed are those who saw you, and those who have fallen asleep in love; for we too shall surely live.

**48:12** Elijah was wrapped in the whirlwind, and Elisha was filled with his spirit; throughout all his days he was not shaken by any ruler, and no one brought him into subjection.

**48:13** Nothing was too great for him, and in death his body prophesied.

**48:14** In his lifetime he performed wonders, and in his death his deeds were marvelous.

**48:15** Despite all this the people did not repent, and they did not turn from their sins, until they were carried off as plunder from their land and were scattered over all the earth.

**48:16** Only a small remnant of the people was left, and a ruler from the house of David. Some of them did what was pleasing to God, but others multiplied sins greatly.

**48:17** Hezekiah fortified his city and brought water into its midst; with iron tools he bored through the rock and built reservoirs for the water.

**48:18** In his days Sennacherib came up and sent Rabshakeh, then withdrew; he raised his hand against Zion and made great boasts in his arrogance.

**48:19** Then their hearts and hands trembled, and they were in anguish like women in labor.

**48:20** But they called upon the merciful Lord and spread out their hands toward him; and the Holy One quickly heard them from heaven and delivered them by the hand of Isaiah.

**48:21** He struck the camp of the Assyrians, and his angel destroyed them.

**48:22** For Hezekiah did what was right and walked steadfastly in the ways of David his father, as Isaiah the great prophet had commanded him, trustworthy in his vision.

**48:23** In his days the sun went backward, and he added years to the king's life.

**48:24** By a great spirit he saw the last things, and comforted those who mourned in Zion.

**48:25** He revealed things to come until the end of time, and hidden things before they came to pass.
